WEB SYNTH v0.9.6 - User Manual [ Close ]

Quick Start

Click Start to initialise the audio engine. Then play by:

  • Computer keyboard: press keys on the C3–C#4 range (keys shown in manual)
  • Mouse / touch: click or drag across the on-screen piano keyboard
  • MIDI controller: toggle the MIDI ON button, then play on your hardware
  • Record: press the REC button in transport, play, press again to save as WAV

Keyboard Shortcuts

A=C3W=C#3S=D3E=D#3 D=E3F=F3T=F#3G=G3 Y=G#3H=A3U=A#3J=B3 K=C4O=C#4L=D4P=D#4 ;=E4
SpacePlay/Pause Sequencer EscapeStop Sequencer .Arpeggiator On/Off (dot key) RStart/Stop Recording (with Ctrl) +/-Octave Shift ?Show Help

Arpeggiator

The arpeggiator plays the currently held chord as a pattern of individual notes. Activate with ARB button or key . (period key). Use the dropdown to set pattern direction, select note rate (1/1 to 1/32) for arpeggiator speed, and the octave selector (+/-2 octaves) to transpose. The ARP button cycles through the 8 built-in patterns.

Chord Mode: Hold 3+ keys simultaneously to form a chord, then activate the arpeggiator. Works in both mono and poly mode.

Signal Flow

osc -> VCA -> filter -> dist -> delay -> master -> reverb -> output

LFO1 -> filter envelope or pitch (selectable)

LFO2 -> filter envelope or pitch (selectable)

Oscillator Panel

  • Saw — Harmonically rich, aggressive. Great for leads, bass, brass.
  • Sqr — Hollow, woody timbre. Organ-like tones, retro game sounds.
  • Sin — Pure, clean fundamental. Sub-bass, soft ambient tones.
  • Tri — Warm, rounded, fewer harmonics than saw/square.
  • Noise — Real white noise buffer via AudioBufferSourceNode. Percussion, wind, texture sweeps.

Glide (Portamento): Time in seconds for pitch slides between consecutive notes. 0 = instant change. Affects keyboard, mouse drag, and sequencer playback.

Sub Oscillator

A second oscillator layered below the main oscillator for extra low-end weight. Toggle ON/OFF with the button. Controls: Vol (mix level 0-1), Oct (-1 or -2 octaves below), Detune (±100 cents for chorus effect).

Filter Panel

  • LP (Lowpass) — Passes frequencies below cutoff. High resonance (>8) creates "squelch" sound.
  • HP (Highpass) — Passes frequencies above cutoff. Removes low end.
  • BP (Bandpass) — Passes a narrow band around cutoff. High Q narrows the band.
  • Notch — Rejects a narrow band around cutoff. Phaser-like effect.

Cutoff: Filter cutoff frequency (20Hz – 18kHz). Res (Q): Resonance boost near cutoff. Q=0 flat, Q=4-6 subtle, Q=8-12 squelch, Q=15+ self-oscillates.

Envelope (ADSR)

  • A (Attack): Time from silence to peak (ms).
  • D (Decay): Time from peak down to sustain level (ms).
  • S (Sustain): Sustained level while key held (0-100%).
  • R (Release): Time from key-off to silence (ms).

F-Env (Filter Envelope): In the LFO panel, sets filter cutoff modulation. Positive values open filter on attack (classic bass "bark"). Negative values close filter.

LFO1 / LFO2

LFO1: Modulates filter or pitch with wave shape (sine/tri/sqr/saw). Rate (0.01-20Hz) controls oscillation speed. Depth (0-100%) sets modulation amplitude. Target = Filter (wah-wah) or Pitch (vibrato).

LFO2: Second independent LFO with same controls. Use both simultaneously for complex multi-dimensional modulation: LFO1 on filter at 1Hz, LFO2 on pitch at 0.2Hz.

Distortion

Waveshaper distortion inserted after the filter. Controls: Drive (0-1, intensity), Tone (0=darker to 1=full spectrum), ON/OFF toggle.

Delay

Delay processor with feedback loop.

  • D-Time: Delay interval (0.01-2s). Sync mode snaps to BPM subdivisions.
  • D-Fdbk: Feedback level (0-95%). More feedback = more repeats.
  • D-Wet: Delay wet mix (0-100%). 0% = dry only.
  • D-Sync: Tempo sync ON/OFF. Synced delay aligns to BPM subdivisions.

Reverb

Convolution reverb with algorithmically generated impulse response. The Reverb wet slider (0-100%) controls mix level. Low (0-20%) = room, Mid (30-60%) = hall, High (70-100%) = cathedral.

Piano Roll

Click a grid cell to place a note, drag across cells to paint a phrase, or click a blue note to erase it. Playback runs left to right in sixteen sixteenth-note steps. Click a piano-key label to hear that pitch.

The lightweight roll is monophonic: each step holds one pitch. Live keyboard playing and manual recording still work separately.

RowLabelControlUse
1ON/OFFToggle buttonEnable or mute this step
2GlideToggle buttonPortamento to next pitch
3ProbCycle: -/…/~/>Probability: off/33%/66%/100%
4RatCycle: -/2x/3xRatchet: repeat notes within a step
5PitchDropdownNote selection (C1–E4)

Swing: Adds groove by shifting even steps later and odd steps earlier. 0 = straight, 10-30 = subtle groove, 30-60 = pronounced funk, 60+ = heavy dub/reggae swing.

Arpeggiator Patterns

  • Up — Ascending chord notes
  • Down — Descending chord notes
  • UpDown — Ascending then descending
  • DownUp — Descending then ascending
  • Random — Randomized chord notes
  • Custom 1/2 — Dynamically generated from current voicing

Chord Mode: Hold 3+ keys simultaneously to form a chord, then activate arpeggiator. Works in both mono and poly mode.

Visualizations

Oscilloscope shows the real-time audio waveform as the synth plays. Spectrum Analyzer shows frequency content with 25 color-coded bars: green = normal level, orange = active range, red = clipping.

Polyphonic Mode

Toggle POLY for polyphonic mode with up to 8 simultaneous voices. Each voice is independent with its own oscillator, VCA, filter env, and sub osc. In monophonic mode (default), the synth plays only one note with glide/portamento between pitches.

Presets

Save, load, export, and import up to 64 preset slots in browser localStorage. SAVE stores current state to the selected slot. LOAD restores it. EXPORT downloads a .json file. IMPORT loads a .json file.

MIDI

Bi-directional MIDI support. When MIDI ON is active: incoming MIDI note-on/note-off messages trigger synth voices through ADSR envelopes and effects. MIDI out sends note-on/note-off when you play via keyboard, mouse, or sequencer. Octave shift applies to both input and output.

Record Session

The REC button captures either live keyboard playing or piano-roll playback as a 16-bit WAV. Press it once to start and again to stop, then press Send to Audacity. The WAV goes directly to Audacity's shared imports folder and is not downloaded to your device. Shortcut: Ctrl+R.

Mixing & Sound Design Tips

  • Bass: Saw + cutoff ~800 + Res ~8 + F-Env +4000 + sub ON + short decay
  • Pad: Tri + cutoff ~3k + A 800ms + S 0.8 + R 1.5s + delay wet 20%
  • Lead: Saw + F-Env +3000 + dist drive 0.3 + LFO 5Hz on filter
  • Ambient: Tri + cutoff 1k + high Res + LFO filter 0.5Hz + delay wet 60%
  • Pluck: Saw + cutoff 4k + Res 3 + A 5ms + D 150ms + S 0
  • Reverb tips: Low (0-20%) for subtle room, Mid (30-60%) for concert hall feel, High (70-100%) for cathedral/stadium
  • LFO layered: LFO1 on filter (wah-wah) at 1Hz + LFO2 on pitch at 0.2Hz sine for organic wobble
